claims.subject: work:rosenzweig_scarcity_2003
claims.statement: Rosenzweig treats digital abundance and the danger of record loss as simultaneous problems for historical research.
claims.qualification: Opening programme in an authorized transcription; not evidence of a complete digital historical record or of current preservation conditions.

claims.subject: work:rosenzweig_scarcity_2003
claims.statement: Rosenzweig argues that historians share responsibility for digital preservation and its social and institutional choices.
claims.qualification: Attributed 2003 programme, not a new legal claim or a statement that archivists lack expertise.

claims.subject: work:gallini_noiret_digital_2011
claims.statement: Gallini and Noiret frame digital history around research, communication, preservation and teaching, and ask how digital media change historical practice.
claims.qualification: Spanish original pp. 16–17; English paraphrase. This Colombian dossier is an intervention, not proof of one Latin American consensus or a founding date.

claims.subject: work:gallini_noiret_digital_2011
claims.statement: Gallini and Noiret connect digital historical communication to collaborative design and translation between historical and technical expertise.
claims.qualification: Spanish original pp. 17–18; a programme for collaboration, not an attribution of all technical work to historians or a claim that digital history replaces older inquiry.

claims.subject: work:winters_web_archives_2018
claims.statement: Winters distinguishes the broad practices of digital history from historians’ more limited engagement with web archives and digital preservation.
claims.qualification: Repository manuscript pp. 4–6; her 2018 assessment, not a current census or an equivalence between digital history, web history and digital humanities.

claims.subject: work:winters_web_archives_2018
claims.statement: Winters warns that curated access routes can privilege particular kinds of web evidence and shape the histories researchers write.
claims.qualification: Repository manuscript pp. 7–9, selected British Library/Archive-It examples; no global archive-coverage estimate or present-day collection count.

claims.subject: work:ogden_maemura_go_fish_2021
claims.statement: Ogden and Maemura distinguish orientating, auditing and constructing as overlapping practices for research with national web archives.
claims.qualification: Selected introduction/framework passages; a comparative conceptual framework from two cases, not a universal linear workflow.
claims.locator: Publisher HTML sections 1 and 3, lines 80–85 and 108–118

claims.subject: work:ogden_maemura_go_fish_2021
claims.statement: Ogden and Maemura show how access arrangements, curatorial labour and collection histories shape possible research questions in UK and Danish web archives.
claims.qualification: Selected 2018 fieldwork accounts published in 2021. Access/legal descriptions are historical observations, not current access advice; two cases do not represent every archive.

claims.subject: work:hegarty_platformization
claims.statement: Hegarty attributes gaps and uneven access in Australian social-media archives to different collection strategies and changing platform constraints.
claims.qualification: Indexed author abstract only; two Australian library cases. No detailed findings beyond that abstract, and no claim that all national archives behave alike.
claims.locator: Publisher abstract, sentences on National Library of Australia crawling and State Library of New South Wales APIs

claims.subject: work:hegarty_platformization
claims.statement: Hegarty explicitly adapts Ann Stoler’s attention to archival form and placement to interpreting platform-mediated web collections.
claims.qualification: Indexed author abstract only; specifically attributed methodological use, not a general Stoler-to-web-history influence arrow or a new reading of Stoler’s book.

claims.subject: work:gibbons_mediated_2026
claims.statement: Gibbons presents mediated recordkeeping and platform paradata as ways to document how archival processes shape evidential meaning.
claims.qualification: Selected introduction/conclusion. The model originated in earlier doctoral research; the 2026 paper presents a diagnostic framework, not a field-tested institutional implementation.
claims.locator: Publisher HTML Introduction lines 65–71 and Conclusion lines 282–288

claims.subject: work:gibbons_mediated_2026
claims.statement: Gibbons argues that making archival gaps visible cannot itself redistribute authority or settle Indigenous sovereignty and community-governance questions.
claims.qualification: Selected limitations/conclusion; a stated boundary of the model, not a claim that technical documentation delivers justice or substitutes for Indigenous-led decisions.
claims.locator: Publisher HTML limitations lines 272–279 and Conclusion line 289

claims.subject: work:leon_2018
claims.statement: Leon links exclusions in digital-history narratives to academic status, institutional location and the invisibility of collaborative labour.
claims.qualification: Selected chapter paragraphs, US-focused argument; her grant tallies are not independently reproduced here or adopted as this graph’s demographic baseline.
claims.locator: Chapter paragraphs on structural labour conditions, extracted lines 183–190
